Fit a Capture-Recapture Model

Source: R/crc_fit.R
crc_fit.Rd

Fits a log-linear capture-recapture model with optional latent classes, misclassification correction for categorical covariates, and a zero-truncated count outcome with missing and censored values. The population size and the outcome total are then estimated with predict.crc_fit().

Usage

crc_fit(
  data,
  captures,
  capture_formula,
  outcome = NULL,
  outcome_formula = NULL,
  outcome_dist = c("ztnegbin", "ztpois"),
  misclass = NULL,
  latent_classes = 1L,
  control = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table with one row per observed unit, i.e., each unit must be captured by at least one source.

captures

A one-sided formula with at least two capture indicators joined by +, e.g., ~ source_1 + source_2 + source_3. The indicators must be numeric or logical, coded as 0/1, and contain no missing values. With two sources, a warning is issued because the number of unobserved units is identifiable only under restrictive assumptions.

capture_formula

A one-sided formula specifying the log-linear model for the expected counts in the cells of the complete contingency table cross-classified by capture histories, categorical covariates, and latent classes. The following rules apply:

  • The formula must include an intercept and every capture indicator as a main effect.

  • Other variables must be factor or character columns without missing values. Unused factor levels are dropped, and character variables are converted to factors with sorted levels (for misclassified variables, the levels follow the confusion matrix).

  • Terms must be untransformed variable names or their interactions (written with :), and every component of an interaction must also appear as a main effect.

  • Capture indicators may interact with each other, and each of them individually with .latent, but not with other covariates.

  • The special term .latent denotes the latent class. It must be included as a main effect when latent_classes > 1 and cannot be used otherwise. .latent is a reserved name and cannot be a column of data.

outcome

Either NULL (no outcome model), a single column name, or a named character vector c(lower = "lower_column", upper = "upper_column"). The outcome is a count variable taking values in \(\{1, 2, \ldots\}\).

  • If a single column name is given, the column must be numeric, its non-missing values must be positive integers, and NA denotes a missing outcome.

  • If lower and upper bounds are given, both columns must be numeric, and for each unit either both bounds are NA or both are observed. Lower bounds must be positive integers, upper bounds must be positive integers or Inf, and lower bounds must not exceed upper bounds. The status of each outcome is determined as follows:

    • both bounds NA – missing outcome,

    • lower == upper – exactly observed outcome,

    • upper == Inf – right-censored outcome, i.e., the outcome is at least lower (e.g., lower = 2 and upper = Inf represent "2 or more"),

    • otherwise – interval-censored outcome, i.e., the outcome lies between lower and upper (inclusive).

Missing and censored outcomes are assumed to be missing or coarsened at random given the variables in outcome_formula. At least one outcome must be observed or censored.

outcome_formula

A one-sided formula with an intercept for the logarithm of the mean of the untruncated outcome distribution. It may contain only variables from capture_formula other than the capture indicators, .latent (when latent_classes > 1), and their interactions (whose components must also appear as main effects). It must be supplied when outcome is not NULL and must be NULL otherwise.

outcome_dist

The zero-truncated outcome distribution: "ztnegbin" (zero-truncated negative binomial, the default) or "ztpois" (zero-truncated Poisson). For "ztnegbin", the untruncated distribution has mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\mu + \sigma \mu^2\), where \(\sigma > 0\) is a dispersion parameter.

misclass

NULL (no misclassification) or a named list with one element per categorical variable subject to misclassification. Each name must be a column of data used in capture_formula or outcome_formula, and that column must be a factor or a character vector without missing values. Each element is a list with the following components:

  • matrix – a square confusion matrix whose row and column names contain the same category levels in the same order. Rows correspond to true categories and columns to observed categories, i.e., the element [g, h] is the probability of observing category h when the true category is g. Entries must be finite and non-negative, and each row must sum to 1. All observed levels of the variable must appear in the matrix. The row names define the true categories used in the model.

  • true_if (optional) – a one-sided formula with capture variables joined by +, e.g., ~ source_1. Units captured by at least one of these sources are treated as correctly classified, i.e., their observed category is taken as the true category. The confusion matrix applies to all other units. If true_if is omitted, it applies to all units.

Confusion matrices are treated as known (e.g., estimated beforehand from an independent validation sample), so their estimation uncertainty is not propagated. For several variables, the misclassification mechanisms are assumed to be conditionally independent given the true categories.

latent_classes

A positive integer giving the number of latent classes. The default 1L corresponds to a model without latent classes. For latent_classes > 1, initial class weights are random, so use set.seed() for reproducible results.

control

NULL or a named list controlling initialization and model fitting. If NULL, the default values are used. Supported elements are:

  • init_alpha: A finite positive number controlling the concentration of the symmetric Dirichlet distribution used to initialize latent-class weights. The default is 20.

  • em: A named list with max_iter, the maximum number of EM iterations (default 1000L), and tolerance, the convergence tolerance (default 1e-6).

  • capture: A named list with max_iter, the maximum number of iterations used in the capture-model M-step (default 100L), and tolerance, its convergence tolerance (default 1e-8).

  • outcome: A named list with max_iter, the maximum number of iterations used in the outcome-model M-step (default 1000L), and relative_tolerance, its relative tolerance (default 1e-8).

Unknown control elements are rejected.

verbose

A logical value indicating whether progress information should be displayed during model fitting. The default is FALSE. Currently unsupported.

Value

An object of class "crc_fit", i.e., a list with the following components:

  • call – the matched call,

  • data – the input data,

  • em_fit – the results of the EM algorithm: capture_fit and outcome_fit (the final capture-model and outcome-model fits with their coefficients; outcome_fit also contains the dispersion sigma for "ztnegbin" and is NULL without an outcome model), state_weights (the posterior state probabilities), cell_counts (the expected cell counts), iterations, converged, and convergence (the final changes used in the stopping rule),

  • model_matrices – the cell grid, design matrices, and expanded states,

  • initialization – the initial state weights and cell counts,

  • captures, capture_model, outcome, outcome_model, and misclass – the parsed model specifications,

  • outcome_dist, latent_classes, control, and verbose – the fitting settings, with control completed with default values,

  • fitted – TRUE for a fitted model.

References

Baffour, B., Brown, J. J., and Smith, P. W. F. (2021). Latent class analysis for estimating an unknown population size – with application to censuses. Journal of Official Statistics, 37(3), 673–697. doi:10.2478/jos-2021-0030

Brännäs, K. (1992). Limited dependent Poisson regression. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series D (The Statistician), 41(4), 413–423. doi:10.2307/2349006

Struzik, A. (2026). Estimation of job vacancy statistics under misclassification and missing data using capture-recapture. Royal Statistical Society 2026 International Conference, Bournemouth, United Kingdom. https://github.com/OJALAB/misclassCRC/blob/main/references/Struzik-RSS-2026.pdf

See also

Other fitting functions: predict.crc_fit(), print.crc_fit(), print.summary.crc_fit(), summary.crc_fit()

Examples

set.seed(123)
N <- 1000
population <- data.frame(
  source_1 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.5),
  source_2 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.4),
  source_3 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.3),
  group = sample(c("a", "b"), N, replace = TRUE)
)
population$outcome <- 1 + rpois(N, ifelse(population$group == "a", 1, 3))

# Keep only the units captured by at least one source
sources <- c("source_1", "source_2", "source_3")
data <- population[rowSums(population[, sources]) > 0, ]
data$outcome[sample(nrow(data), 50)] <- NA

fit <- crc_fit(
  data,
  captures = ~ source_1 + source_2 + source_3,
  capture_formula = ~ source_1 + source_2 + source_3 + group,
  outcome = "outcome",
  outcome_formula = ~ group
)
fit
#> Capture-recapture model fit
#> 
#> Observed units:          791
#> Capture sources:         source_1, source_2, source_3
#> Latent classes:          1
#> Misclassified variables: none
#> Outcome distribution:    zero-truncated negative binomial
#> EM algorithm:            converged after 34 iterations
predict(fit, by = ~ group)
#> Capture-recapture prediction
#> 
#> Population size:         1,020
#> Outcome total:           2,978
#> Grouping variables:      group
#> Groups:                  2
#> 
#> Grouped estimates:
#>     group population_size outcome_total
#>    <fctr>           <num>         <num>
#> 1:      a           499.0         980.1
#> 2:      b           520.9        1998.2
